<h3><span style="color: #000000"><strong>From the Seller</strong></span></h3>
<div>
<p><strong>What are the operating procedures for running this business?</strong></p>
<p>--The site’s content strategy is built around three main types of posts: educational content, freebie posts, and affiliate marketing posts.</p>
<p>For the educational content, I initially developed a content silo focused on helping parents and educators teach young children foundational skills. The content begins with early concepts such as learning the alphabet and numbers, then progresses into handwriting, early literacy, and other skills that help prepare children for kindergarten. Before creating new content, I research current teaching methods, topic ideas, and relevant keywords. I then use SEO best practices to structure and write each post.</p>
<p>I use AI primarily as a writing and organizational assistant to help structure posts, improve clarity, and make sure the content flows naturally. Every post is reviewed and edited so it sounds helpful and personable rather than automated or robotic. Once a post is published, I share it across my social media platforms and promote it to my email list.</p>
<p>Freebies are also an important part of the operating strategy. I regularly create small printable resources based on seasons, holidays, or popular educational topics. These freebies are promoted through blog posts, social media, and email marketing to attract new visitors and grow the subscriber list.</p>
<p>For affiliate content, I review offers available through my WarriorPlus account, along with educational resources and programs created for homeschooling families. <p>For my own digital products, I typically create the product first, then develop a related freebie that introduces readers to the topic or provides a smaller sample of the solution. I then publish supporting blog content, promote the product through email and social media, and create a sales funnel designed to generate both direct product sales and follow-up funnel sales.</p>
<p>Overall, the business follows a connected content system in which educational posts, freebies, affiliate recommendations, digital products, social media, email marketing, and sales funnels work together to build traffic, grow the email list, and generate revenue.</p>

<p>If I were keeping the site, I would continue using the same overall content and monetization strategy while increasing the consistency of promotion and audience growth.</p>
<p>Over the next three to six months, I would focus on publishing more educational content within the existing content silos, creating seasonal and evergreen freebies to grow the email list, and developing additional digital products that connect naturally with the blog content. I would also continue creating affiliate posts around carefully selected educational and homeschooling resources that would be useful to the site’s audience.</p>
<p>A major focus would be growing the site’s Pinterest presence. I would create fresh pins for both new and existing blog posts, pin content several times each week, and build out relevant boards around preschool learning, kindergarten readiness, educational printables, seasonal activities, and homeschooling resources. I would also continue sharing content across the site’s other social media platforms to increase visibility and bring more visitors back to the website.</p>
<p>I would review the site’s highest-performing posts and update them with stronger keywords, improved internal linking, fresh images, relevant freebies, affiliate recommendations, and product offers. I would also create additional supporting posts around topics that are already bringing in traffic.</p>
<p>For digital products, I would continue using a connected funnel strategy by creating the product first, developing a related freebie, publishing supporting blog content, and promoting the offer through email, Pinterest, and social media. I would also build or improve automated email sequences so new subscribers are introduced to relevant content, products, and affiliate offers over time.</p>
<p>The overall goal would be to increase traffic through consistent SEO content and Pinterest promotion while improving income through digital products, affiliate commissions, email marketing, and stronger sales funnels.</p>

<p>Through support, communication, and an abundance of ideas to help keep the relationship thriving, this relationship and lifestyle site is an incredible go-to source for all couples. And now the creator is looking for a new owner to continue to grow and develop the site and its devoted audience.</p>
<p>The business boasts <strong>387 articles,</strong> <strong>strong organic traffic </strong>and a <strong>decade-old aged domain</strong>. Monetized through a premium ad network, the site <strong>averages $557 a month</strong> on autopilot.</p>
<p>The seller notes the revenue model is straightforward, scalable, and does not rely on active selling. The blog operates as a largely passive digital asset and requires minimal ongoing management.</p>
<p><strong>The site is packed with 387 articles with a strong focus on marriage. </strong><strong>Articles cover:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Date night ideas</strong></li>
<li><strong>Anniversary and Holiday ideas</strong></li>
<li><strong>Couple's Travel</strong></li>
<li><strong>Marriage advice and tips, including</strong>
<ul>
<li><strong>implementing daily practices</strong></li>
<li><strong>checking in </strong></li>
<li><strong>communication</strong></li>
<li><strong>building a support system</strong></li>

<p style="font-weight: 400"><strong>What are the operating procedures for running this business?</strong></p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">Ongoing operational requirements are limited to:<br>

<p style="font-weight: 400">The site is currently stable and does not require daily oversight.</p>
<p style="font-weight: 400"><strong>If you were going to keep the site, what steps would you take over the next 3 to 6 months to grow the income and traffic?</strong></p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">The site already receives the majority of its traffic from Pinterest, which validates both the niche and the visual content strategy.</p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">If retained, I would focus on scaling that channel further.</p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">Key actions would include:<br>
• Creating additional fresh, keyword-optimised pins for top-performing posts<br>

• Implementing consistent pinning focused on seasonal trends<br>
• Updating older pins with improved keyword targeting<br>

<p style="font-weight: 400">With structured optimization and consistent execution, Pinterest presents a clear opportunity to increase traffic and revenue within 3–6 months.</p>

<p style="font-weight: 400">The site uses Grow’s Automailer, which requires no manual email management.</p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">Automailer sends a digest email every 7 days (adjustable), featuring post images, titles, and snippets from both new and evergreen content.</p>
<p style="font-weight: 400">This provides automated re-engagement without ongoing input.</p>

<p style="font-weight: 400">For selected roundup posts, I used AI tools to assist with drafting introductions and conclusions. All content was personally reviewed, edited, and finalised prior to publication.</p>

<p><b>What are the operating procedures for running this business?</b></p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">One of the things I love about this site is that it doesn't require a ton of daily maintenance.</p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">The business is pretty straightforward to run, which is one of the reasons I've enjoyed owning it.</p>
<p>Most of the day-to-day work involves creating and publishing content, sending emails to subscribers, creating Pinterest pins, and promoting products to the audience. I also check in on site performance, update older content when needed, and occasionally add new products to the shop.</p>

<p><strong>If you were going to keep the site, what steps would you take over the next 3 to 6 months to grow the income and traffic?</strong></p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">Honestly, I think there's still plenty of room for growth.</p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">If I were keeping the site, I'd focus on publishing more content around topics that are already performing well, increasing Pinterest activity, and growing the email list with additional freebies and opt-in offers.</p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">I'd also spend time adding new affiliate opportunities and creating a few simple digital products that align with what the audience is already looking for.</p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">I'll also implement additional email automation sequences to increase subscriber engagement and conversions</p>
<p>The foundation is there. It simply needs someone with the time and focus to continue building on it.</p>
<p>The truth is, I haven't been able to give this site the maximum attention. Between work, family, and other projects, I've focused on maintaining it rather than aggressively growing it. That's why I think it's a great opportunity for someone who wants to step in and build on what's already been created</p>
<p>I'll continue maintaining the site and keeping everything running as normal while it's listed for sale. My goal is to ensure a smooth transition and preserve the value of the business for the new owner.</p>

<p>The list has been an important part of building trust with readers and driving repeat traffic back to the site.</p>

<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">The audience is primarily made up of entrepreneurs, creators, small business owners, and people looking for practical tools to help them grow their businesses. Products such as templates, toolkits, planners, and business resources have consistently been the strongest revenue drivers.</p>
<p class="gmail-isSelectedEnd">Affiliate income is an additional revenue stream, but product sales generate the majority of the revenue.</p>
<p>One of the things I like most about the business model is that each new product creates another opportunity to generate revenue from both existing subscribers and new visitors.</p>

<h3><b>Q&A with the Seller</b></h3>
<p><strong>Operations</strong></p>
<p><strong>What are the operating procedures for running this business?</strong></p>
<p><em>For movies I get emails about them coming out: whether it is streaming, DVD, BluRay, 4K etc, or if it is coming to the theater, or Hulu, Amazon.  I post what they send as they give what you can write, assets like posters for Pinterest, featured images you can resize, YouTube videos you can embed etc. Then I post them to my Socials and send the links to the HR that sent the email to me.</em></p>
<p><em>Then there are ones that send you a "Code" for the movie and you redeem it on Movies Anywhere, watch it, and review it and send the links to the person who sent you the code.  You do not have to do every movie-but do the ones you like.</em></p>
<p><em>You can also do giveaways (TallGirlPR) usually sends these and they provide and send to the winners. So you just hold the giveaways--and sometimes or most of the time they offer the movie to you (usually in either DVD or digital code for hosting it).  </em></p>
<p><strong>For Books:</strong></p>
<p><em>I have been posting the Press Release with a small blurb at the top about how the book seems exciting then the press release, a link to purchase it on Amazon. ONCE I have the author or the Press place agree to send me a physical book in exchange for the coverage on my site and my socials.  I say if I am able I will read the book and include a review at a later time but I do not promise.  I always include my address when I pitch them for the exchange so they are able to send the physical book without tons of back and forth.</em></p>
<p><strong>If you were going to keep the site, what steps would you take over the next 3 to 6 months to grow the income and traffic?</strong></p>
<p><em>I would probably include more reviews on shows I watch on Netflix, Hulu or another streaming service so people might have a go to list of what to watch if they are looking for a new show.</em></p>
<p><em>For something to sell possibly do patterns (digitally) for bookmarks that people could purchase to make their own. Or printables for their kids to keep them busy.  Because you can't make Disney characters etc you would have to figure out something else or branch out for something for their Mom's to do to keep the kids busy.  That is where I fell short and have not came up with something myself.  </em></p>
<p><strong>Where is your site currently hosted, and where are the domain names currently registered?</strong><br>
<em>My site is currently hosted with New Blog Hosting. </em><em>Domains are hosted at <a href="https://name.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow">https://name.com</a>.</em></p>
<p><strong>Email Marketing</strong></p>
<p><strong>How often do you email your list? </strong></p>
<p><em>Every day whatever is posted is set up to automatically send a full day of posts to my subscribers the next morning.</em></p>

<p><em>MailPoet Pro.</em></p>
